content: Healthcare professionals are encouraged to develop and provide educational materials that are culturally tailored to meet the needs of patients who do not speak English. These materials should specifically focus on promoting awareness and prevention of diabetes. The National Standards for Culturally and Linguistically Appropriate Services (CLAS) serve as a framework to help reduce language barriers and improve cultural competency among healthcare providers. These standards emphasize the importance of ensuring access to language assistance services, which can significantly enhance the quality of care delivered to individuals who are not proficient in English.
